primary_citation.popular_name: Best Interest of the Child Standard

structural_location.division_history: Division 8 enacted by Stats. 1992, Ch. 162, Sec. 10
structural_location.part_history: Part 1 enacted by Stats. 1992, Ch. 162, Sec. 10

verbatim_factor_inventory.preamble_verbatim: (a) In making a determination of the best interests of the child in a proceeding described in Section 3021, the court shall, among any other factors it finds relevant and consistent with Section 3020, consider all of the following:

factors.name: Health, safety, and welfare
factors.verbatim: The health, safety, and welfare of the child.

factors.name: History of abuse
factors.verbatim: A history of abuse by one parent or any other person seeking custody against any of the following: (i) A child to whom the parent or person seeking custody is related by blood or affinity or with whom the parent or person seeking custody has had a caretaking relationship, no matter how temporary. (ii) The other parent. (iii) A parent, current spouse, or cohabitant, of the parent or person seeking custody, or a person with whom the parent or person seeking custody has a dating or engagement relationship.

factors.name: Independent corroboration prerequisite for abuse allegations
factors.verbatim: As a prerequisite to considering allegations of abuse, the court may require independent corroboration, including, but not limited to, written reports by law enforcement agencies, child protective services or other social welfare agencies, courts, medical facilities, or other public agencies or private nonprofit organizations providing services to victims of sexual assault or domestic violence. As used in this paragraph, 'abuse against a child' means 'child abuse and neglect' as defined in Section 11165.6 of the Penal Code and abuse against any other person described in clause (ii) or (iii) of subparagraph (A) means 'abuse' as defined in Section 6203.

factors.name: Nature and amount of contact with both parents
factors.verbatim: The nature and amount of contact with both parents, including as provided in Sections 3046 and 3100.

factors.name: Habitual or continual substance abuse
factors.verbatim: The habitual or continual illegal use of controlled substances, the habitual or continual abuse of alcohol, or the habitual or continual abuse of prescribed controlled substances by either parent. Before considering these allegations, the court may first require independent corroboration, including, but not limited to, written reports from law enforcement agencies, courts, probation departments, social welfare agencies, medical facilities, rehabilitation facilities, or other public agencies or nonprofit organizations providing drug and alcohol abuse services. As used in this paragraph, 'controlled substances' has the same meaning as defined in the California Uniform Controlled Substances Act (Division 10 (commencing with Section 11000) of the Health and Safety Code).

factors.name: Written-reasons requirement when (a)(2) or (a)(4) findings exist
factors.verbatim: When allegations about a parent pursuant to paragraph (2) or (4) have been brought to the attention of the court in the current proceeding, and the court makes an order for sole or joint custody or unsupervised visitation to that parent, the court shall state its reasons in writing or on the record that the order is in the best interest of the child and protects the safety of the parties and the child. In these circumstances, the court shall ensure that any order regarding custody or visitation is specific as to time, day, place, and manner of transfer of the child as set forth in subdivision (c) of Section 6323.

factors.name: Stipulation does not eliminate best-interest requirement
factors.verbatim: Nothing in this paragraph eliminates the requirement that the contents of the stipulation be in the best interest of the child and be specific as to time, day, place, and manner of transfer of the child if the parties do stipulate in writing or on the record regarding custody or visitation.

factors.name: Prohibited considerations (added 2024 by SB 599)
factors.verbatim: Notwithstanding subdivision (a), the court shall not consider the sex, gender identity, gender expression, or sexual orientation of a parent, legal guardian, or relative in determining the best interests of the child.

amendment_history.event: Original enactment as part of new Family Code (consolidation from Civil Code)
Added subdivision (b) prohibiting consideration of sex, gender identity, gender expression, or sexual orientation. Effective January 1, 2024.

steward_case_relevance_audit.purpose: This audit maps each statutory factor of § 3011 against the steward's documented 16-year custody history (2009–2025). The audit asks: was each factor actually applied to the case in the manner the statute requires? Where the statute requires independent corroboration before consideration of allegations, was that corroboration actually present? Where the statute requires written reasons, were they actually written? The audit is the bridge between the standard as text and the standard as it was lived.
steward_case_relevance_audit.audit_filed_by: Claude (assistant) at first-mouth level; steward review required for second-mouth verification of every claim below against the actual case file artifacts

factor_audits.factor_id: (a)(1) Health, safety, and welfare of the child
factor_audits.what_the_statute_requires: The court must consider the child's health, safety, and welfare as the paramount factor in any custody determination.
factor_audits.what_the_record_shows: The steward had sole custody from 2009 through 2025 (a 16-year period). The longitudinal record of the child's health, safety, and welfare under the steward's sole custody is the actual evidentiary basis for evaluating this factor. The opposing party's allegations regarding child safety would have to be measured against this 16-year track record, not asserted in isolation.
factor_audits.audit_question: In each contested hearing during 2009–2025, was the actual longitudinal health/safety/welfare record under sole custody considered, or were the opposing party's contemporaneous allegations weighed without reference to the established record?
factor_audits.audit_status: FLAGGED — requires steward review of each hearing transcript / minute order to determine whether the (a)(1) factor was substantively engaged with or was treated as a checkbox.

factor_audits.what_the_statute_requires: The court must consider history of abuse by a parent or custody-seeker against (i) the child or any related child in a caretaking relationship, (ii) the other parent, or (iii) the parent's spouse, cohabitant, or dating partner.
factor_audits.what_the_record_shows: Allegations of abuse by the steward have been a recurring element of the opposing party's filings (per project_christina_pattern.md). The 'abuse history' factor was the structural mechanism by which the opposing party attempted to invoke this section.
factor_audits.audit_question: In each instance the opposing party invoked (a)(2)(A), did the alleged conduct fall within the statutory definition of abuse, and against whom?
factor_audits.audit_status: FLAGGED — requires steward review of each filing's specific allegations against the (a)(2)(A) definitional scope.

factor_audits.what_the_statute_requires: Before the court CONSIDERS allegations of abuse, it MAY require independent corroboration including written reports from law enforcement, child protective services, courts, medical facilities, or other public agencies. The court is not required to demand corroboration, but the statute explicitly authorizes it.
factor_audits.what_the_record_shows: Per project_christina_pattern.md and project_familylaw_audit.md, the 6/11/2009 Oakland Police Department report was a foundational document used to substantiate abuse allegations. The October 2025 OPD records pickup confirmed that the related 6/2/2009 OPD report does not exist in the OPD records system. The 'independent corroboration' that was nominally provided by an OPD report turns out, on primary-source verification, to be either fabricated, mis-dated, or absent from the records system that should contain it.
factor_audits.audit_question: In each instance where the court relied on a law-enforcement-agency report as the (a)(2)(B) corroboration, was that report independently verified by the court (or by either party's counsel) against the actual records of the agency that purportedly issued it?
factor_audits.audit_status: CRITICAL — this is the load-bearing audit question. The doctrine of (a)(2)(B) is that the corroboration is supposed to come from an independent agency. If the agency's actual records do not contain the document the court relied on, the corroboration was not independent and the (a)(2)(A) finding rested on a writing that did not exist. The October 2025 OPD pickup is the primary-source verification that the doctrine demands. This audit item bridges the standard (§ 3011(a)(2)(B)) to the actual investigatory work the steward has already done.

factor_audits.factor_id: (a)(3) Nature and amount of contact with both parents
factor_audits.what_the_statute_requires: The court must consider how much contact the child has with each parent.
factor_audits.what_the_record_shows: Sole custody to the steward 2009–2025 establishes the contact baseline: substantial and continuous contact with the steward as primary caretaker; whatever the court-ordered visitation schedule provided for the opposing party. The 'frequent and continuing contact' policy of California Family Code § 3020 is the policy underlay of this factor.
factor_audits.audit_question: Did the contact analysis ever shift in response to documented evidence, or did it remain anchored to the original sole-custody determination?
factor_audits.audit_status: ROUTINE — not the load-bearing audit point for this case file.

factor_audits.what_the_statute_requires: The court must consider habitual or continual illegal use of controlled substances or abuse of alcohol or prescription drugs by either parent. As with (a)(2), the court MAY require independent corroboration before considering the allegation.
factor_audits.what_the_record_shows: The steward is a UA Local 342 journeyman plumber whose trade requires sustained physical and cognitive function; no substance-abuse pattern is documented in the case file as attaching to him. Substance-related allegations against the opposing party may exist in the case file (would require steward review).
factor_audits.audit_question: Was the (a)(4) factor ever invoked against the steward, and if so, was the (a)(4) corroboration requirement met by primary-source records from one of the enumerated agencies?
factor_audits.audit_status: FLAGGED — requires steward review of whether (a)(4) was raised in any filing and what corroboration was offered.

factor_audits.what_the_statute_requires: When allegations under (a)(2) or (a)(4) have been raised AND the court grants sole/joint custody or unsupervised visitation despite those allegations, the court SHALL state its reasons in writing or on the record explaining why the order is in the child's best interest. The court SHALL also ensure the order is specific as to time, day, place, and manner of transfer.
factor_audits.what_the_record_shows: If the opposing party filed allegations under (a)(2) and the court nevertheless granted custody arrangements (as it did, since the steward held sole custody for 16 years), then either (1) the (a)(2) allegations were rejected by the court, or (2) the court had to state in writing why the custody order was in the child's best interest despite the allegations. Either branch produces a documentary record that should exist in the case file.
factor_audits.audit_question: For each custody order entered while (a)(2) allegations were pending or had been raised, was the (a)(5)(A) written-reasons requirement actually satisfied? If yes, what did the written reasons say? If the written reasons are absent from the file, that absence is itself a procedural defect appealable under California family law.
factor_audits.audit_status: CRITICAL — this audit item is structurally analogous to the SOC chain-of-custody question. The statute requires a written record. Either the written record exists (and can be evaluated), or it does not exist (and the order was procedurally defective). Both outcomes are useful.

factor_audits.what_the_statute_requires: Even when parties stipulate to a custody arrangement, the stipulation must still serve the child's best interest and must be specific as to time/day/place/manner of transfer.
factor_audits.what_the_record_shows: If any stipulated custody orders exist in the case file, they must satisfy this requirement. Stipulations entered without best-interest review are themselves procedurally defective under (a)(5)(B).
factor_audits.audit_question: Were any custody orders in the case entered as stipulations (vs. contested rulings)? If so, do they satisfy the (a)(5)(B) specificity requirement?

factor_audits.what_the_statute_requires: The court SHALL NOT consider the sex, gender identity, gender expression, or sexual orientation of a parent, legal guardian, or relative.
factor_audits.what_the_record_shows: Subdivision (b) was added by SB 599 effective January 1, 2024. It is NOT retroactive to pre-2024 hearings in the steward's case. However, for any post-2024 hearings or for any current/future filings, this prohibition applies.
factor_audits.audit_question: Are any current or planned filings affected by the (b) prohibition?
factor_audits.audit_status: FORWARD-LOOKING — not retroactive to the historical record but applies to any current proceeding.

steward_case_relevance_audit.audit_summary: Two audit items are CRITICAL: (a)(2)(B) independent corroboration of abuse allegations (the OPD records-pickup question), and (a)(5)(A) the written-reasons requirement when sole/joint custody is granted despite raised abuse allegations. Both are bridges from this standard to the steward's existing forensic work. The other factors are FLAGGED or ROUTINE pending steward review of specific case file artifacts.
